themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing Across District
themes_detail.summary: Nine missing street sign complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 2300% spike (z-score: 17.82)—suggesting either systematic theft, vandalism, or installation failures that could impact navigation and traffic safety in Murray Hill/Gramercy.
evidence: 9 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 17.82, severity: high)
2300% spike represents sharpest statistical deviation in current dataset
Pattern emerged suddenly with no gradual escalation over prior 8 weeks
reporting_angles: Ground canvass: which intersections are missing signs and for how long?
DOT follow-up: are signs being stolen, damaged during construction, or failing to install?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 75 THIS WEEK from 20.4 weekly average—a 268% spike (z-score: 5.26)—indicating a sudden wave of pothole, pavement, or sidewalk damage reports concentrated in the past 7 days.
evidence: 75 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.26, severity: high)
268% spike aligns with recent winter weather and thaw cycle typical for NYC
Consistent with recurring community board budget request for DOT funding, suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Identify geographic clusters: are specific avenues (Park Ave South, 3rd Ave) hit harder?
DOT repair timeline: how long are complaints sitting in queue before repair crews respond?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Three cannabis retailer complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either new unlicensed dispensaries opening or increased enforcement focus in Murray Hill/Gramercy.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
2300% spike emerged this week with zero complaints in prior weeks
Likely connected to state enforcement actions or new retail openings in neighborhood
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations: are unlicensed shops clustering near schools, residential areas, or transit hubs?
Interview residents and CB members: what are the specific complaints (odor, youth access, storefront conduct)?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Chaos (Recent Peak)
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints peaked at 92 THREE WEEKS AGO (445% above 16.9 weekly average, z-score: 14.23), and Taxi Report complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK (540% above 0.6 baseline, z-score: 6.97), pointing to ongoing transit-for-hire friction in the district.
evidence: For-hire vehicle complaints: 92 filed 3 weeks ago vs. 16.9 weekly average (445% spike, z-score: 14.23)
Taxi report complaints: 4 filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 6.97)
Two-pronged spike (both for-hire and traditional taxi) suggests congestion or driver behavior escalation
reporting_angles: Interview TLC enforcement and Uber/Lyft on surge complaints in neighborhood (illegal parking, double parking, blocking fire hydrants?)
Ride-hail driver interviews: are there surge pricing or demand patterns driving aggressive behavior?

themes_detail.label: Damaged Trees + Vendor Enforcement Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 8 LAST WEEK (967% above 0.8 baseline, z-score: 7.49) and vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK (167% above 4.5 baseline, z-score: 4.01), suggesting either weather damage or street management crackdowns.
evidence: Damaged tree complaints: 8 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Vendor enforcement complaints: 12 THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average (167% spike, z-score: 4.01)
Tree damage likely tied to winter weather; vendor spike may reflect enforcement campaign or street activation projects (POPS plazas in pipeline)
reporting_angles: Parks/DEC interview: which streets have the most tree damage and what is restoration timeline?
SBS/enforcement interview: what triggered vendor enforcement increase—is this linked to new POPS activations or illicit vending crackdown?
